content: 1. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of antidepressants when co-administered. It is essential to carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. Start with the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitor the response closely, especially when used with SSRIs and cobicistat. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 3. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 4. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of atazanavir. Monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 6. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Cobicistat and fosphenytoin are contraindicated together. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406, the active metabolite of fostamatinib, necessitating dose adjustments to prevent toxicities. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction of fostamatinib. 9. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 10. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of ganaxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, changes in ganaxolone exposure with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. Monitor closely. 11. Garlic decreases the levels of atazanavir through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. 13. Cobicistat and atazanavir significantly increase the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects and adjust dosage as needed. 15. Atazanavir and gilteritinib co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used due to increased levels of gilteritinib. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects and adjust dosage as needed. 16. Atazanavir and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Use caution, monitor closely, and obtain ECGs during initiation and co-administration. Withhold treatment if QTc > 500 ms or if there is a > 60 ms change from baseline. 17. Cobicistat and atazanavir significantly increase the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 18. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Clinical trials have shown increased risk of ALT elevations with this combination. 19. Atazanavir decreases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 20. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. Reduce guanfacine dosage to half the recommended dose if co-administered. 23. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cobicistat and atazanavir significantly increase the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 29. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. 30. Atazanavir significantly increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust dosage as needed. 31. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 32. Atazanavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, and insulin lispro due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution, modify therapy, and monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 33. Atazanavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
